summary: Added an OS-managed single-writer lock to the resumable raw-chat importer and a lock-exclusion regression test.
facts: tools/resumable_chat_import.py now wraps the import operation with an exclusive lock on the output directory.
A second process using the same local output directory is intended to fail visibly instead of concurrently mutating the same SQLite state.
The lock is managed by the OS and should be released when its owning process exits; the persistent lock file is not itself the lock.
The regression test checks that a second lock acquisition fails while held and that acquisition succeeds after release.
The Linux/Unix fcntl path is the CI target; Windows msvcrt behavior and network filesystems are not separately tested.
This change is newer than EVT-AGMS-20261018-001 by Git commit ancestry. Exact-head CI for the newest change and checkpoint commits was pending at the time this event was written.
hypotheses: The directory-level lock should serialize cooperating processes that use the same local output directory, but does not provide distributed locking or guarantee lock semantics on every network filesystem.
action_taken: Added a cross-platform lock context manager, routed import_export through the lock, added a regression test, and documented the lock/platform boundary in core/source_ingestion_protocol.md.
outcome: A local single-writer guard is implemented and has a targeted test; exact-head CI and Windows/network-filesystem behavior remain to be verified.

summary: Added a fail-closed append-only event writer that validates temporal relations before writing.
facts: tools/append_memory_event.py adds append_event_record(journal_path, record, trusted_order).

The writer reads the existing JSONL journal, rejects duplicate event IDs, validates the complete temporal graph using the supplied trusted order and append-only correction overlays, and only then appends the new record under an OS-managed exclusive lock.
After appending, the writer flushes and fsyncs the file. Validation errors leave the journal bytes unchanged.
The CLI accepts a journal path, a JSON file containing one event, and a JSON mapping of event IDs to trusted integer order.
Tests cover invalid edge rejection without mutation, valid append, duplicate ID rejection, correction overlay handling, and missing chronology.
The validator also rejects booleans as chronology ordinals even though bool is a Python int subtype.
The writer has not yet been run against the full existing AGENT_MEMORY_SYSTEM/events.jsonl because a complete trusted-order mapping for all legacy temporal edges has not been assembled.
hypotheses: The fail-closed writer provides a safe path for future event appends once the caller has a complete trusted chronology map; legacy journals with unresolved temporal edges will require explicit reconciliation before this writer can append to them.
